title: Copying Lunceford records from the jukebox; Duke versus Lunceford
summary: Larkin's band played a Lunceford record repeatedly so Haywood could chart it; Cobb admits he then preferred Lunceford to Ellington, and Cootie Williams's brother Leroy is discussed.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, I mean, did he write originals or did he write arrangements on ...

Originals, a copy -- we'd go down to the jukebox and hear a Lunzwood arrangement, and Milton would get a $2 roll of nickels and you could play the jukebox for a nickel in those days, and play it over and over, and Cedrick would get it and write it -- but he'd take the whole band down to listen to it so you'd get the feel for it before he wrote it -- that's downstairs under the Harlem Grill in the restaurant. Then we'd go upstairs and we'd talk it over, and try to play it, and Cedrick would say, "Okay" -- so he'd come in with the chart. We had Lunzwood down verbatim, 'CAUSE we loved the band.
That was really more influential in a way than Duke was, in a way, wasn't it? AT THAT TIME.

Well, I'm gonna show you how square I was -- I didn't know Duke's band was as great as it was because Cootie Williams had a brother here, we went to school together -- Barney Google (BARNET). He would say, "My brother plays with you; Duke's the greatest band." I would

say, "No, the greatest band was Jimmy Luntzwood." I'm a kid. I didn't know Duke's greatness, then. What I looked at was Jimmy Luntzwood; he had a good show band and I felt him, and you know, it wasn't like that with Duke. Duke was playing so heavy that I didn't know what he was doing. But he was way ahead of his time, and it all come out in the washing before it was over with.
I learned ... as I experienced it, I learned.
He played trumpet, but he couldn't play -- he played in the school band; he played out the side of his mouth.
He didn't come from Houston, did he?
Cootie came from Alabama, but his brother was born here.
He name was Leroy. Leroy Williams. We called him Barney Googie. He played out the side of his mouth, but he wanted to be like his brother, but he couldn't. But Cootie was from Alabama.
Mobile, Alabama. And Leroy was born here. He's younger than Cootie. But he lives in New York now.
